text:
Marathon Petroleum fell a flat 0.08% today, but what matters is the two-week collapse of 10.65%—most of that damage came on November 4th and 5th when crude oil prices dropped sharply. The trigger was renewed hope for a ceasefire in Iran, with President Trump saying the conflict would end "fairly soon" and Brent crude briefly dipping below $90 a barrel for the first time since August. Lower oil prices directly squeeze refiner profits because they reduce the value of the fuel these companies produce and sell.

The stock has stabilized over the last two trading days, hovering near $390, even though crude remains pressured by ongoing peace negotiations. Refinery utilization is still robust at 94.5%, which normally supports margins, but storage levels for gasoline and diesel are elevated—suggesting either weak demand or abundant supply coming to market. Until oil prices stabilize or geopolitical tensions flare again, refiners like Marathon face headwinds from the combination of lower crude and plentiful inventory.
